newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE Central Bank urges bourse open to foreigners.
newsitem.headline: UAE Central Bank urges bourse open to foreigners.

text.p: The UAE Central Bank has proposed to the cabinet that foreigners be allowed to own up to 49 percent of companies listed on the long-awaited official stock market, its governor said on Sunday.

"We proposed allowing foreigners to own a percentage of local shares not exceeding the 49 percent allowed to foreigners under the company law," Sultan Nasser al-Suweidi told reporters on the sidelines of a meeting of Arab finance ministers and central bankers.
"A draft law prepared by the Central Bank is one of three submitted to the cabinet," he added.
About three-quarters of the UAE's 2.4 million people are foreigners who have been excluded from the market.
For years, the UAE has been working on setting up an official exchange to replace the current system of trading through a handful of brokers and banks.
Last week, Dubai's Emirates Bank International (EBI) said it would launch in June the country's first equity fund, which would allow 20 percent foreign ownership.
